messages.subject: Error loading rstan in RStudio
parts:
I'm not sure if this is most relevantly posted here, or on an RStudio list, but I get an error when trying to load rstan in RStudio, and only RStudio.

If I start up the regular R GUI, or run R from the terminal, I get this:

> library(rstan)
Loading required package: Rcpp
Loading required package: inline
Loading required package: RcppEigen
Loading required package: Matrix
Loading required package: lattice
rstan (Version 1.0.1, packaged: 2012-09-12 01:55:01 UTC, GitRev: 2d5ac1828e4d)

But if I try it in RStudio, I get this:
> library(rstan)
Loading required package: Rcpp
Loading required package: inline
Loading required package: RcppEigen
Loading required package: Matrix
Loading required package: lattice
Error in dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...) : 
  unable to load shared object '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.15/Resources/library/rstan/libs/x86_64/rstan.so':
  dlopen(/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/2.15/Resources/library/rstan/libs/x86_64/rstan.so, 6): Symbol not found: ___emutls_get_address
  Referenced from: /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.6.dylib
  Expected in: /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/lib/libgcc_s.1.dylib
 in /usr/local/lib/libstdc++.6.dylib
Error: package/namespace load failed for ‘rstan’

In all three cases, it's definitely the same version of R running underneath:
R version 2.15.1 (2012-06-22) -- "Roasted Marshmallows"
Copyright (C) 2012 The R Foundation for Statistical Computing
ISBN 3-900051-07-0
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin9.8.0/x86_64 (64-bit)

Is this an rstan issue, or should I go post this to RStudio's lists?


Thanks
-Joe

reason I don't usually work with IDEs like RStudio or
Eclipse.

I don't see how you could get 32-bit R inside a new
Mac OS X release, as it's all 64-bit these days.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error loading rstan in RStudio
parts:
I am not working on this right now as it seems not to be a RStan problem intrinsically. 
But probably I should take a look to see I can figure it out. 

But generally, if both 32-bits and 64-bits version of RStan need to be installed, 
you can add option in the following instead to install rstan, which would almost double the installation time. 

install.packages('rstan', type = 'source', INSTALL_opts = "--merge-multiarch")

Using the above, at least for me, I found no problem on both terminal and R app for both 32 bits and 64 bits.

Personally, I would use only 64 bits just on terminal. 

Jiqiang

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Error loading rstan in RStudio
parts:
I will write some in the instruction for RStudio users. 

What is more, please check if R_ARCH is set if you want to install rstan in RStudio.  If it is not, for some reason, function install.packages will take my 64bits RStudio as 32bits and then compile 32bits RStan.  I guess then it is problematic to load rstan. 

So if using RStudio, the first thing to do after start RStudio is to check R_ARCH is set appropriately.  I strongly recommend at least installing rstan in official R app's. 


--
Jiqiang
